crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: The AI Enablement Audit
children.blurb: The AI Enablement Audit is a structured review that clears an organization to deploy AI systems by checking security, privacy, intellectual property, and regulatory compliance.

children.name: Threat Modelling for Legal AI
children.blurb: Threat modelling for legal AI is the structured practice of identifying, prioritising, and mitigating threats to AI systems used in legal work, including legal research, drafting, contract review, e-discovery, and matter management.

children.name: Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation
children.blurb: Data loss prevention and sanitisation in AI covers the controls that keep sensitive data from leaving an organisation through prompts, outputs, training pipelines, retrieval stores, logs, and agent actions.

children.name: Shadow AI in Legal Teams
children.blurb: Shadow AI in legal teams covers any use of artificial intelligence tools by lawyers, paralegals, legal operations staff, or outside counsel without review or approval from the firm's or department's security, privacy, and legal operations functions.

children.name: Bias Testing and Alignment
children.blurb: Bias testing and alignment covers the measurement of how a model's outputs differ across groups and the work of steering those outputs toward stated goals and policies.

sections.body: AI security audits and enterprise enablement is the work of letting legal teams use AI tools without losing control of data, privilege, or client confidences. In practice, firms run enablement audits to inventory which models and assistants staff already use, then set rules for approved use. Threat modelling for legal AI maps how a model could leak a draft, hallucinate a citation, or be manipulated through a poisoned document. Data loss prevention and sanitisation tools strip client identifiers before text reaches a third party model, and they log what leaves the firm. Shadow AI in legal teams is the unsanctioned use of chatbots and summarisers, often on personal accounts, which bypasses those controls. Bias testing and alignment work checks whether a model treats similar matters differently because of names, language, or jurisdiction, and whether its outputs follow firm policy.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is partly solved at the level of policy and inventory, because firms can now list approved tools and block some network traffic. It is not solved at the level of proof, because no audit can guarantee that a model will not memorise or reconstruct confidential text. Case law is still thin, with 29 AI case law precedents tracked on this site, so many risk decisions rest on regulation and contract rather than courtroom guidance. The pressure is real, with 148 active AI lawsuits tracked here and 92 of them intellectual property disputes, which shows how quickly AI use turns into legal exposure. Bias testing remains hard because legal harm is context specific, and a model that passes a general fairness test may still fail on a specific client matter. Honest limits include incomplete model transparency, fast changing tools, and the fact that an audit is a snapshot, not a permanent guarantee.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The AI Enablement Audit is the starting point for a firm that needs to know what AI is already in use and what controls exist. Threat Modelling for Legal AI then turns that inventory into specific attack paths, such as prompt injection, data exfiltration, and citation fabrication. Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation covers the technical and procedural filters that keep privileged material out of external systems. Shadow AI in Legal Teams addresses the human side, including personal accounts, unapproved plugins, and the gap between policy and daily practice. Bias Testing and Alignment gives the reader methods for checking model behaviour against firm values and client expectations. Together these pages move from discovery to design to monitoring, and a reader can use the site's 219 compliance and regulation pages for the wider rule context that surrounds them.
